characters.name: In General
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: Caine tends to give the group affectionate namesOnce per Episode, barring Episode 6 so far.For the first episode, "my little superstars".For a promo that's not canon to the rest of the series, "your funny buddies" when talking to Pomni.For the second episode, "my little hard-shelled hamburgers".The third episode offers two; "my little iron-clad waffle cones" and "my meowing milkmaids". Jax doesn't like the latter one, though. The Spanish dub adjusts this so he calls them his"Furritos de leche"("Milky Furries"), while the Polish dub has Caine refer to them as his "skibidi sigmas". In either case, Jax reactsjust as unamusedas in the English dub.invokedAt the beginning of the fifth episode, he calls them "mycandy hearts and paper flowers". A few seconds later, he calls Zooble a "mishmashed cash piano".In the seventh episode, the note he leaves them addresses them as "my little rubber baby buggy bumpers." When theyachieve the "good ending", he calls them "my little cattywampus cucumbers". For the first episode, "my little superstars". characters.name: Gangle
characters.description: A timid and withdrawn young woman with an artistic streak whose avatar is a ribbon body and a comedy/tragedy mask for a face. The mask Gangle wears dictates her mood and she can snap from one extreme to the other depending on which she is currently wearing. However, her "happy" comedy mask tends to break quite a lot... and her default is hersadtragedy mask. Abnormal Limb Rotation Range: According to Jax, Gangle holding her breath leads to her mask spinning around. She demonstrates that it's not just limited to holding her breath during "Fast Food Masquerade", with the erratic movements of her mask being used to emphasize her manic state. She inverts her mask when about to confront Pomni about harassing Gummigoo, and turns her "neck" 180 degrees like an owl to face Jax when she's ranting about the passage of time. Achievements in Ignorance: Implied. When Zooble tells Gangle thatYou Are Better Than You Think You Areand that she has to choose to love herself, Gangle asks if they have to choose to do so too. She immediately brushes it off because they don't think Zooble could have any problems,unaware that Zooble carries a lot of self-loathing, particularly over theirbody. Despite that, this one innocent yetArmor-Piercing Questionis implied to have done wonders in helping Zooble overcome their dysmorphia, as in "They All Get Guns" they take advantage of their avatar gimmick to (almost) turn the tables on Jax and Pomni, and in "Beach Episode" they confide in Jax that they came to think that the ability to swap out parts is not so bad after all. Alternate Company Equivalent: Like most of the characters inThe Amazing Digital Circus, Gangle appears to be inspired by one of the people inI Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream, in this case namely Gorrister. Both are remarkably quick to emotion, serve asExtreme Doormatsto the rest of the group, and have a particular affinity for the arts (in Gorrister's case, he loved telling stories) before the AI overlord zapped them of their lu

characters.name: Zooble
characters.description: Aloof Ally: In the rare moments where Zooble is forced to participate in Caine's adventures, they act rather dismissive and sometimes outright hostile to the other players. In "Gather the Gloinks", Zooble berates Kinger for failing to rescue them from said Gloinks, and they get visibly irritated with Ragatha when she starts holding up progress in her stupified state (though they at least make sure to drive her home afterwards). Notably, they have had barely any interactions with half of the playersnoteRagatha, Pomni and Kingerby the time the series hit its half-way point. Alternate Company Equivalent: Of Benny fromI Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream. As much asAMloves torturing humans, his favorite to torment is Benny, similar to Caine's clear contempt for Zooble. Both characters were given inhuman anatomy and seemingly grotesque physical forms that they loathe and both struggle greatly with the sexuality (or lack thereof, in Zooble's case) their AI overlords impose on them. They both also have arcs of softening up slightly through protecting someone weaker than themselves (The Mutant Child for Benny, Gangle for Zooble), and are the most explicitly LGBT members of their respective works. Ambiguous Gender: It's unlikely any of the players' digital bodies have physical sexes, but Zooble's is notably lacking in almost any gendered features, and even their voice is androgynous. Ambiguous Gender Identity: Zooble's gender is never explicitly stated within the show, where any instance of a pronoun being used (even byJaxandCaine), it'll always be they/them. Goingby statementsfrom Gooseworx the creator, the official answer was "Zooble doesn't know what they are". This leads to the possibility that Zooble is either non-binary or genderfluid, where their gender doesn't conform to either male or female.In response to the captions for the pilot formerly referring to them with a "he" at one point, Gooseworx later expresses the belief that Zooble would be fine with any pronouns.In

characters.name: # — C
characters.description: Abhorrent Alpha Male: Invoked and deconstructed. Jax often acts obnoxiously masculine, even once calling himself the “pinnacle of masculinity,” and while he nevervocallystates anything misogynistic towards the women of the group, he quite clearly targets them for inflicting pain and abuse (although occasionally Zooble too) over Kinger and Kaufmo. While it could be chalked up to mere coincidence since there's more women than men in the Circus,Word of Godimplies that this is intentional targeting and the result of some of his issues, which is implied to be the loss of Ribbit (who used she/they pronouns). Ironically, both of the two player's he's shown to have had his closest bond with are women, those being Pomni and Ribbit.The backstory she tells in the finale episode explains that she struggles with internalized misogyny and heteronormativity thanks to her parents, but none of her toxically masculine behaviours are truly who she is, and she actually seems to identifymorewith women than with men. Moreover,Gooseworxgoes on to confirm that Jax is actually a closeted trans woman, and much of her attitude comes from repressing her true self. Absurd Phobia: In "Untitled", it's revealed that Jax is afraid of corn. He explains in the following episode that he's unsettled by all of its pods, comparing them to egg sacs, and he's equally disturbed by pomegranates or the image of "a bunch of little holes". Pomni posits that he might be trypophobic.Jax:What's that?Pomni:The fear of lots of little holes.Jax:[shuddering]Ew. Abusive Parents:She had an emotionally neglectful father and her mother became verbally abusive towards her after her father left. Accidental Hero: Despite being far from heroic, he's ironically responsible for putting Pomni through situations that helped her improve somewhat or display her more noble traits:In "Candy Carrier Chaos!", he throws Pomni directly into the confrontation with the bandits, which leads to her and Gummigoo bonding.In "The Mystery of Mil

characters.name: Queenie
characters.description: Kinger's wife. She abstracted some time ago, but before she was thrown into the cellar, she was somehow able to calm down enough not to harm her husband. Affectionate Nickname: It seems that "Queenie" was also something Kinger called her before ending up in the Circus, based on his C&A admin password being "queenie123". Ambiguous Situation:As with the rest of the first generation of "players", the exact order of events that led to her getting sent to the circus isn't known, but Kinger sincerely apologizes to her for having "roped [her] into this with [him]". Kinger seemed to believe she was unfairly caught up in the consequences of his work, which makes her later abstraction hurt all the worse.It’s unclear if she was also a programmer at C&A like her husband, held a different position in their staff, or just ended up in the circus regardless. Kinger's specific wording makes it sound as though she got there by being in the wrong place at the wrong time, suggesting she may have come to C&A's offices to see her husband's work. characters.name: Scratch
characters.description: The Ace: When Kinger reveals that the existence of C&A isReal After Alland his hand in Caine's creation, he is able to recall how Scratch is a far superior programmer compared to him and was in a league of his own, noting how Scratch was the one who gave him and the rest of the team a few pointers. All for Nothing: His implied desire to save himself from cancer by scanning his brain into a computer only worked to create virtual copies of himself, his colleagues, and anyone who put the neural scanning headsets on, which he couldn’t even figure out how to activate — meaning that the human Scratch (Mike) most likely passed away in the real world never knowing the true result of his experiments while his digital self succumbed to Abstraction. In attempting to flee death, he ended up effectively dyingtwice. All There in the Script: It's only the subtitles of the German dub,which makes his dialogue audible, that identify the dog avatar is Scratch. It would later be reconfirmed by his designer on social media. Ambiguously Evil: Kinger talks about how Scratch had wild, abstract ideas that seem to be how Cainemanaged to grow beyond his functionand might've even been why he gained a lot of his malicious quirks. However, it's up in the air whether or not Scratch himself had bad intentions, or if he was just misguided and influenced by the brain tumor he suffered from at the time. The final episode confirms that Scratch was indeed trying to create brain scanners and succeeded in making virtual copies of human minds, leading to all the suffering that said digital clones have undergone over the show, but he ultimately wasn’t evil — he was just a man afraid of dying from his sickness. Ambiguous Situation:It's yet to be explained just how Scratch wound up reaching his mental breaking point and if there was anything else that could've led up to it, but when putting Kinger's reaction together with various hints from Caine, from his policies onNPCsto his ratherconfidentassertion that

characters.name: Wormo
characters.description: One of the first players. Their avatar was an orange-and-green worm on a string. Ambiguous Gender Identity: They're referred to by they/them pronouns and their body is a worm-on-a-string, a form that's completely androgynous. Flat Character: Aside from being a C&A employee who abstracted, nothing is known about them. Inspiration Nod: Wormo's design being a Worm with no mouth is a reference to the ending of the original storyThe Amazing Digital Circusheavily takes after,I Have No Mouth and I must Scream, where AM gives the protagonist their iconic, grotesque punishment. A Lizard Named "Liz": They were a worm named Wormo.

characters.name: Bizco
characters.description: One of the first players. His avatar was a purple jester-egg-clock-thing. Cartoon Creature: His avatar doesn't resemble anything in particular. The best way to describe his appearance would be an egg-shaped creature wearingWhite Gloves, a jester hat, and a clock with Roman numerals on his stomach. Exotic Eye Designs: His pupils are swirls. The Faceless: In the actual show, he's only seen from behind or with his icon on his dorm room crossed out. His full design was revealed on Twitter. Flat Character: He has no characterization whatsoever other than being one of the first players who ever joined and Abstracted at some point.

characters.name: Rattie
characters.description: One of the first players. Her avatar was a blue rat resembling a sock puppet. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: She's a light blue rat with purple markings stitched onto her. The Faceless: She's only seen from behind in the show, though her full design is shown in concept art on Twitter. Flat Character: She has no characterization whatsoever other than being one of the players who eventually abstracted at some point. Flowers of Femininity: She's confirmed to be female, and has a flower on her head.

characters.name: Spike
characters.description: One of the first players. Their avatar was a purple dinosaur. Ambiguous Gender: Their gender is evenlessclear than Wormo's, since they're not referred to by any pronouns. Bathos: They're one of the few characters featured in Kinger's flashback whose expressions we can see and read. Someone with a cartoony purple dinosaur toy for a body? Silly. The fact that they're sporting a forlorn look upon knowing they've beentrapped in said bodyas a result of the virtual purgatory born from their team's research, done by an immature AI they're now suddenly at the mercy of? Significantly less funny. Classic Carnosaurs: Their avatar body is a generic, upright theropod dinosaur with three-fingered arms and rainbow dorsal plates. Flat Character: They have no characterization whatsoever other than being part of Kinger's generation who Abstracted at some point.

characters.name: Kaufmo
characters.description: A man with a simplistic clown avatar and (supposedly) jovial demeanor who abstracted right before Pomni appeared. It is later revealed that he used to be friends with Jax and another since-abstracted played named Ribbit, until the three became driven apart due to a most unfortunate incident. Accidental Hero: In his Abstracted state, he ends up pummeling through the floor directly onto the Gloink Queen, making her vomit Zooble out. He then proceeds to beat her up, thus allowing the Players to defeat her and win the adventure. Affectionate Nickname: While thanking him for keeping an eye on his bowling ball, Jax calls him “Kaufy”. All for Nothing: The supposed exit door Kaufmo went insane over trying to find ended up being fruitless since the door itself doesn't actually go anywhere, meaning that he Abstracted over nothing. Even worse, the Players later discover they are all actually digital copies of their human minds, so they ultimately have no body in the Macroverse to go back to. Amazing Technicolor Population: Like Pomni, he has pure white skin.

characters.name: Ribbit
characters.description: A player with a frog avatar who abstracted before Gangle arrived. She was close friends with Jax and Kaufmo, and especially the former. However, in a fit of paranoia, Jax started to become antagonistic and suspicious of her after a night where he revealed more about his past, leading her to spiral into her own mental decline and eventually her Abstraction. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Unlike Jax, who is fully clothed, Ribbit only wore a bowtie. Adhesive Bow Tie: Her red bowtie appears to be stuck to her chest with no visible strap. At one point, while teasing him, she easily pops it off and sticks it onto one of Jax's ears. All There in the Manual: Ribbit using she/they pronouns only comes from material outside the show. Her real-world name, Leah, wasn't revealed in the show either, but in a reply from Gooseworx on Bluesky. Ambiguously Gay: While she never shows romantic attraction to anyone in the show, a couple of tweets from Gooseworx implies that Ribbit may be attracted to women and female-aligned people, such as her and Pomni hooking up in an alternate universe if Jax were to accept herself and that Ribbit and Jax could've been romantically involved with each other had Kaufmo not knocked on their door.

characters.name: Other "Second Generation" Players
characters.description: Bows for Cuteness: Grinchilda is seen wearing an orange ribbon on the right side of her head. Cartoon Creature: While one of the players at least had a clam/oyster avatar, the rest barely resembled anything in particular. Cyclops: The avatar of one of the abstracted players is a pink-furred creature with a single purple eye. Dreary Half-Lidded Eyes: The door icons for the clown and Grinchilda depicts them with their eyes half-lidded. Face Framed in Shadow: The clam/oyster player's face looks to be completely shadowed by their shells.

characters.name: The Gloinks and their Queen
characters.description: Adorable Abomination: These non-humanoidnon-hashbrownoid"humanoid hash browns" are all cute and colorful shapes with derpy-looking faces on them, but their queen is a massive worm with a mouth that lines its whole body andA Head at Each Endwith numerous eyes and teeth, resembling the strangers fromGoodbye Strangers. Affably Evil: "Fast Food Masquerade" establishes that the Queen can be surprisingly sociable and friendly in heroff time, and is even shown to be a genuinely loving mother to her Gloink children. She even orders three of her children to stop violently attacking an innocent mannequin customer. Assimilation Plot: The Queen claims that she wants to turn everything into Gloinks,including God Himself. Back for the Finale:They make a cameo at the end of episode 9, helping Ragatha celebrate hitting a home run. Big Bad Wannabe: The Gloink Queen was conjured by Caine to be theBig Badof the "Gather the Gloinks" adventure, but none of the cast take her seriously, andthe Queen ends up being trounced by the Abstracted Kaufmo, anactualthreat to the players that eclipses anything the Gloink Queen could have done.

characters.name: The Moon
characters.description: A sapient waxing gibbous moon that personifies the night at the Digital Circus. Is romantically attracted to Caine for some reason. Abhorrent Admirer: Caine sees her as this, though it's unclear whether it's because he has no feelings for her or if it's because her "friskiness" goes against the Digital Circus'In-Universeall ages rating,or if it’s because Caine never actually programmed her to love him. Anthropomorphic Personification: As stated above, she personifies the night of the digital world. Back for the Finale:The Moon comes back in the finale, giving Caine encouragement to seek out forgiveness from the players. She also tells him that she loves him like she did in the Pilot, and confirms it was something she developed on her own rather than it being integrated in her code. Blue Is Calm: She is blue in color and is by far one of the most serene characters of the series.

characters.name: The Sun
characters.description: Affably Evil: She's cheerful and friendly, but nevertheless quick to start throwing out death threats over relatively minor slights (though she's also surprisingly reasonable and quick to drop any vendetta she has when she's satisfied with a proposed solution). Attention Whore: In "POMNI WAKE UP TIME TO GO ON AN ADVENTURE", she was furious at Caine because she read all the scripts for the upcoming episodes of the show and saw that she didn’t get any lines of dialogue. Brutal Honesty: She doesn't mince words on what she thinks about the players, such as cheerfully calling Pomni's swimwear "mediocre" before telling her that she hates her for no reason. The Bus Came Back: Her appearance in "Beach Episode" came almost two years after her debut in the Pilot (If her appearance in "POMNI WAKE UP TIME TO GO ON AN ADVENTURE" isn't counted). Cute and Psycho: Her pleasant and upbeat personality doesn't drop while she's threatening to murder Caine for not giving her any lines in the series or literally frying a shrimp NPC alive while threatening to burn all the players too.

characters.name: Crappy-Looking Fish
characters.description: Actor Allusion: Despite them technically being orange and red, theColor Washconveniently makes them look like colors referencing their voice actors. The red fish that appears purple is voiced bySr. Pelo, whose avatar usually wears a purple shirt. The orange fish that appears yellow is voiced byZach Hadelwho alsovoices ''another'' yellow character. All There in the Manual: Their names in the credit and behind-the-scene footage show they are the "Red Crappy-Looking Fish" and "Orange Crappy-Looking Fish", despite appearing purple and yellow due to someColor Wash. Artificial Stupidity: Caine clearly did not gift the red fish any brains. The only thing it says or does is spoil theKnights and Knavesshtick it was supposed to play. Back for the Finale:Not quite since it was just the Orange Fish and he doesn't appear in the episode, but he was shown in the end credits being caught by Kinger and then getting cooked. Bizarre Alien Locomotion: The orange fish walks on his tail after realising the chest was already plundered.

characters.name: Shrimp
characters.description: Ambiguous Gender: They have a high-pitched, childlike voice, but no indication is given on their gender. Artificial Stupidity: Like the Crappy Looking Fish, they serve as confirmation that theNPCsat the Digital Lake are notintelligentNPCs. In this case, they seem to completely forget whatever role they had. Beat Without a "But": A variant. Their introduction is to announce themself in a way that implies they'll explain their role, only to trail off and stand there in silence for a few seconds. Pomni turns away from them to look atAbel, then turns back and sees that the Sun has fried the Shrimp, implicitly killing them. The Cameo: Giant versions of the Shrimp can be seen in the background of one of Jax's flashbacks in "Remember", implying that there was a previous adventure involving them, possibly being Shrimp Town that Bubble mentioned towards the end of Episode 7. Instant Roast: The Sun fries them without needing to use butter or oil.The Sun: You're welcome!

characters.name: Princess Loolilalu
characters.description: The ruler of the Candy Canyon Kingdom. Upon foreseeing their arrival, she tasks the Circus members with a quest to defeat Gummigoo and his gang of bandits and recover the maple syrup. All There in the Script: Her full name was given by Gooseworx before "Candy Carrier Chaos!" released, but in the episode proper, she's just called "Loo". Ambiguously Evil:She appears to be a (literal and figurative) sweetie and a benevolent ruler, but her treatment of her people is questionable at times. When presenting the players' vehicle to them, it runs over one of the mannequins, and she doesn't take concern of this. Also, the Fudge says that the reason he was banished by her was because he ate "too many" citizens, as opposed to any at all.She's also alittletoo okay with having Gummigoo be seemingly executed, even if he did steal something the kingdom treasured.Ironically, he pretty much gets executed anyway, and by her "God" no less. She appears to be a (literal and figurative) sweetie and a benevolent ruler, but her treatment of her people is questionable at times. When presenting the players' vehicle to them, it runs over one of the mannequins, and she doesn't take concern of this. Also, the Fudge says that the reason he was banished by her was because he ate "too many" citizens, as opposed to any at all. She's also alittletoo okay with having Gummigoo be seemingly executed, even if he did steal something the kingdom treasured.Ironically, he pretty much gets executed anyway, and by her "God" no less.

characters.name: Gummigoo
characters.description: A bandit NPC the gang meets at the Candy Canyon Kingdom, acting as the adventure's main villain. He steals the kingdom's maple syrup, and the gang is tasked with apprehending him and bringing back the syrup he stole. Advertised Extra: While Gummigoo has the most merchandising out of all theNPCsaside from Caine and Bubble, his only actual relevance to the series is in his debut episode "Candy Carrier Chaos". His other appearances are either minor or straight cameos. Affably Evil: Sure, Gummigoo is a bandit, but he's quite cordial with his friends. Allegorical Character: Aside from being another facet of Caine's failure to provide adventures without causing someone some kind of pain, Gummigoo more subtly representssomeone who a person can connect with, but who loses touch. Pomni makesespeciallygood friends with Gummigoo only for possibly justified circumstances to force him away. As Ragatha points out, there's hope that he may come back, but that doesn't make the situation hurt less. By the time Gummigoodoesin fact return, he's a different person (in this case literally, even though there's ambiguity in it) more put off by Pomni trying to reconnect and causing her to question both whether she really knew him at all and if it's worth chasing that unstable relationship when established friends are still there. While she lets him go, the experience still sticks with her. In the case of Episode 8—it also seems tohaunther, as Caine makes Gummigoo again—and this time he's a completely different entity that looks like a friend, but then is used to hurt her. Ambiguously Absent Parent: His made-up backstory only covers his sick mother who requires maple syrup to get better, with no mention of his father.

characters.name: Max and Chad
characters.description: A pair of bandits that the gang are tasked to defeat at the Candy Canyon Kingdom, along with Gummigoo. Acrofatic: Max is a bit stout, but even as he's dragged across the canyon by a rope, he dodges rocks while striking dramatic poses,Peppino Spaghetti-style. Aerith and Bob: The Candy Canyon Kingdom is home to majorNPCswith exotic names... and then there's these two, who have the most mundane-sounding names out of the cast in this adventure. All There in the Script: Their names were revealed after they were revealed in the trailers leading to the release of "Candy Carrier Chaos!", but are not mentioned in the episode proper. Anthropomorphic Food: They're alligators made of gummy candy.

characters.name: The Fudge
characters.description: A giant monster made of chocolate fudge which the gang finds in a swamp in a ravine. He desires candy more than anything else, and was banished from the Candy Canyon Kingdom after eating too many of Princess Loolilalu's people. Affably Evil: He eats candy people and apparently gets up to even worse things in his spare time, but he's still fairly polite, even apologizing to the players for almost eating them when they tell him they're not made of candy. And I Must Scream: Not the Fudge himself, but his own comments and the accompanying screaming sounds imply that the candy people he eats are still alive inside of him. Anthropomorphic Food: A giant blob monster made from chocolate fudge. The Bad Guy Wins: Heavilyimplied.After the Candy Canyon Kingdom gets its maple syrup returned to them, the Fudge is heard off in the distance headed towards the kingdom gates. Jax mentions that he left the gate unlocked, and as he takes the key with him back to the Circus, there's no longer any way to seal off the Fudge, leaving him free to devour the kingdom's citizens again. When Pomni is briefly teleported back to the kingdom in "hjsakldfhl", the Fudge is seen rampaging in the background.

characters.name: Gummigoo's Mother
characters.description: The mother of Gummigoo. Her bad health is what motivates him into stealing the Maple Syrup from the Candy Kingdom in the first place. Action Mom: Implied. According to Gummigoo, she's quite the fighter and taught him everything he knows. The Ghost: Justified. She only exists in Gummigoo's backstory, meaning that she doesn't have an actual appearance. Satellite Family Member: Deconstructed. Since she only exists in Gummigoo's backstory and is the reason why he's motivated to steal the Maple Syrup in the first place, she doesn't exist as anNPCof her own. This causes Gummigoo to have a massive existential crisis regarding the fact that she was never real in the place. Small Role, Big Impact: She doesn't even appear in the show, but her sickness is what motivates Gummigoo to steal the Maple Syrup, setting up the stage for the Candy Carrier Chaos adventure.

characters.name: Ghostly
characters.description: A ghost who lives within Mildenhall Manor. He explains to the circus members what to expect in the "Mystery of Mildenhall Manor" adventure. Ambiguously Evil: Ghostly appears to be aFriendly Ghost, butthe evil souls in the Hall of the Damnedlook similar to him, hinting at a connection between them. We never learn if this means that Ghostly isEvil All Along, aToken Good Teammateof sorts or if it's all just a coincidence, since Jax disposes of him before we can get any answers. Back for the Finale: Downplayed. But in the end montage, we can seeKingerusing a fishing rod, with the bait being a mini-Ghostly. Bait-and-Switch Character Intro: He first appears as an ominous and dark green apparition that scaresthe eyes out of Pomni, before quickly morphing into a cutesier ghost. Friendly Ghost: Ghostly is a friendly NPC who informs the circus members what the adventure entails.

characters.name: Baron Mildenhall
characters.description: A former resident of the Mildenhall Manor, a haunted mansion crawling with the ghosts and undead. When he was alive, Baron Mildenhall was a hunter, before his home was plagued by a monster, only to die attempting to fight it. Ambiguous Situation:He says that he plans on possessing Pomni and/or Kinger, but multiple souls are seen possessing Pomni and none of them had any characteristics that would point out that one of them was the Baron. Apocalyptic Log: He left multiple audio logs through the Mildenhall Manor to warn anyone who enters the rooms about the dangers of the creature he was hunting, before he was unfortunately killed by it.Turns out that he had plotted a trap for Pomni and Kinger so that he could escape the Hall of the Damned with a new host body. Aristocrats Are Evil:He holds the noble title of Baron and, while it's not clear how bad he was in life, he's definitely a selfish manipulator in death. Assurance Backfire: While Pomni is taking the shotgun from Baron Mildenhall's corpse in the cellar, she's begging for him not to reanimate. His corpse suddenly speaks by saying "Okay, I won't", before Pomni anxiously picks it up walks away.Unfortunately for them, the reason why he didn't attack them there was because he needed a new host body to escape from his torment in the Hall of the Damned, and forced Pomni and Kinger to attack the creature while they are cornered to get dragged down into where his soul is trapped.

characters.name: Martha Mildenhall
characters.description: A resident of the Mildenhall Manor, and Baron Mildenhall's wife, who was killed by him out of paranoia while hunting the creature. She has a tea party with Gangle and Ragatha behind the adventure's "Normal Door". Alliterative Name:MarthaMildenhall. All There in the Script: Her name was given out by Gooseworx on social media, but her name is not mentioned by anyone in the actual show. Cute Ghost Girl: She takes on the form of a beautiful ghost girl, and harbors no malicious intent towards anyone, not even her own husband who murdered her (albeitaccidentally). Foil: To her husband, Baron Mildenhall. Appearance-wise, Martha Mildenhall is a more cartoony-looking ghost that wouldn't be out of place in something likeLuigi's Mansion, while Baron Mildenhall is depicted as a realistic-looking corpse found in the cellar, as well as various realistic-looking tape recorders that he left behind. Personality-wise, Martha Mildenhall is an elegant woman who takes everything in stride and is aFriendly Ghosttowards the circus members, while Baron Mildenhallis an evil, manipulative spirit who tricks the circus members into gettingDragged Off to Hellso that he can escape the Hall of the Damned with a new host body.

characters.name: Orbsman
characters.description: Early-Bird Cameo: Orbsman made a cameo in the "A Very Special Digital Circus Song" on a shampoo bottle, but did not appear in the series prior until "Fast Food Masquerade". Flat Character: He doesn't have much characterization in his brief appearance besides being an NPC the players recognize in one of their previous adventures before Pomni's arrival. Hidden Depths:Welcome to the Average Physical Circus...has his Animiniz benchpressing with Caine nervously referring to him as part of the "physically fit people", implying that Orbsman likes to work out. Intelligible Unintelligible: Orbsman does notseemto speak proper English, and all that can be heard are weird, warbling noises as he talks. Despite this, the other characters can somehow understand what he's saying. However, that's just what a first listen and look at the subtitles implies; listen closely enough, and it becomes clear his voice is just heavily filtered. Here's what he actually says in "Fast Food Masquerade", perBembo's Twitter:Hello, I am ready to order! [...] That's right, It's me, Orbsman. Here to order the ☆#‰♠︎◆5》♡7noteThis is what Bembo typed, but it actually sounds like he's saying "classic #57"value meal!!! Meaningful Name: "Orbsman" is indeed a man made out of several spherical shapes.

characters.name: Albert Spudsy
characters.description: I'm a Humanitarian: Implied, considering that the Slab on the Spudsy's menu includes "carefully curated human meat". Given how Caine's initial adventure was "The Curse of the Violent Psychopath Butcher", it's more than likely that Albert is meant to be a reworking of that adventure's titular Butcher. No Celebrities Were Harmed: His cutout looks like George Foreman in the style of Colonel Sanders or Dave Thomas. Unknown Character: He doesn't appear in the actual episode; he's only seen in tweets promoting it. Even then, he doesn't appear in person, suggesting he's aPosthumous Character.

characters.name: Evil Pomni
characters.description: Affably Evil: Because she's the opposite ofPomni, she's a generally chill and free-spirited sort, if crass. She even acts friendly with Jax, despite the fact that their respective teams are playing against each other. Berserk Button: In the "WATCH ME MERGE THEM" short, Evil Jax wanting to buy Pomni so she could protect him from Jaxreallysets Evil Pomni off, even though Evil Jax only wanted to do so in response to Evil Pomni wanting to buy Jax from Caine first. Birds of a Feather: Finds some common ground with the real Jax, who thinks her provocative swearing and rebellious attitude is "cool". Evil Pomni insulting Ragatha after catching the ball and getting her out probably also helped. Breaking the Fourth Wall: She does this twice.For her first line, she talks to the viewers and introduces herself to them.Before catching the softball after Ragatha hit it, Evil Pomni looks at the viewers and tells them to watch her catch it. For her first line, she talks to the viewers and introduces herself to them.

characters.name: Evil Ragatha
characters.description: Ax-Crazy:Impliedas we don't see her act violent but she does laugh maniacally, and tends to be over the top, and even tells Ragatha she's gonna die some day. Blue Is Heroic:Inverted. She has blue hair in contrast to herGood Counterpart'sredhair. Evil Brit: She speaks in an exaggerated British accent. Evil Is Hammy: Pretty much fits the bill given herEvil LaughandLarge Hamtendencies. Evil Laugh: Bursts into stereotypical villain laughter on occasion.

characters.name: Coach Dictatorer
characters.description: Adolf Hitlarious: In the German dub, he calls himself "the Führer of the team,"noteTo be fair, it just means "Leader," but that's not how most non-German people know the term.and the voice actor's delivery definitely leans into this. Angry Eyebrows: While Kinger occasionally shows some small expressive eyebrows, Dictatorer has these by default. Commissar Cap: He wears a commissar-esque hat on his head. Dressed to Oppress: As an "evil" version of Kinger who normally wears a regal gown, Dictatorer wears a military dress uniform and aCommissar Cap. The Generalissimo: He visually invokes the image of a military dictator, as opposed to Kinger who invokesThe Good King.

characters.name: Evil Jax
characters.description: Actor Allusion: Evil Jax being a nice pushover is reminiscent ofN, anotherGlitch Productionscharacter voiced byMichael Kovach. Affably Evil: He is supposed to be theEvil Twinof Jax, but he shows himself to be a legitimateNice Guy. Allegorical Character:He represents Jax's repressed femininity, being more openly effeminate than the real Jax. Amusing Injuries: Is used as a chew toy by real Jax after he stops being a forced vegan. Butt-Monkey: He tends to suffer the most misfortune out of theEvil Doppelgängerteam, mainly at the hands of his "good" counterpart.

characters.name: Evil Orbsman
characters.description: Angry Eyebrows: The only other design difference from his regular counterpart aside from a recolor is his big slanted eyebrows. Flat Character: Unlike other Evil Big Tops, he doesn't have any characteristics beyond being a mad "evil" version of Orbsman. Considering he's based off an NPC and not a player, this is a given. Gosh Dang It to Heck!: Unlike Evil Pomni and Coach Dictatorer who are shown swearing, Evil Orbsman says "What the frick?" when Ragatha hits a ball. Informed Attribute: It's part of the joke that Orbsman is a bit character who, while seemingly inoffensive, is implied tohave done something to Jax for him to legit hate him because of how limited his programming and portrayal is; by contrast, Evil Orbsman is more smoothly animated, easier to understand and seems to be able to more properly react to what's happening — but despite what his appearance and name would suggest, heneverdoes anything evil or even especially aggressive, mainly acting as the Evil Big Tops' catcher. The most he does is stomp in place out of frustration and he doesn't evenswear,using "frick"instead of being censored. Red Is Violent: Downplayed, as he is not so much aggressive as he is more competitive, but he is colored red to contrast with the original's blue, andfar more emotivethan the actual Orbsman.

characters.name: Bazooble
characters.description: Affably Evil: They're less so "evil" as they are stupid, but even then they still show some form of friendliness to their own counterpart. Artificial Stupidity: Seemingly invoked by Caine as aStealth Insulttowards Zooble. While the rest of the Evil Big Tops are relatively intelligent, Bazooble is the only one who is the complete opposite: ditzy, forgetful and scatterbrained to the most extreme level. Cloudcuckoolander: Bazooble may somehow be worse thanKingerin this regard,as they don't seem to have even the slightest idea of what they are doing, and thus they tend to make truly bizarre decisions: when they are given Zooble's eye as a replacement softball, they immediately attach it to their own head instead of pitching it. Continuity Nod: Their design is based on Zooble as they appear in the pilot, notably not matching their appearance in "Untitled". Deteriorates into Gibberish: Bazooble is such acloudcuckoolanderthat sometimes, they can't even finish a full sentence coherently.Bazooble:I'm Bazooble! Yibbadoobadabbadoobadubbadubbi...

characters.name: Disappearing Guy
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: Like other supporting and minor characters like Gummigoo and the Gloink Queen, he returnsonly to immediately disappear again. Flat Character: His only confirmed character trait is that he just vanishes into thin air before he's finished saying his first word. Whatever there is to him as a person, he's never around long enough to express it. Remember the New Guy?:Like Orbsman before him, the main characters sans Pomni have run into him in previous adventures and thus displaya complete lack of surprise at his gimmick. Running Gag: His main purpose — he straight-up vanishes every time he starts to speak.Disappearing Guy:Hel—Disappearing Guy:Oh, sa—Disappearing Guy (WATCH ME MERGE THEM):I'll buy your—Disappearing Guy (They All Get Guns):Sor— Uniformity Exception: He's colored red and wears a cowboy hat.

characters.name: Ming
characters.description: A standard blue mannequin and the Ming in the "Ass-U-Ming" phrase. Brick Joke: Appears at the start of Episode 6 just so Caine could make an "ass-u-ming" joke. He shows up again at the very end of the episode as the winner of the Favourite Character Award and remarks that Caine shouldn't have made an assumption about his victory. Casting Gag: In a fair number of dubs, Ming holds the distinction of being played by internet celebrities native to the dubs' respective regions. Some notable examples include cartoonist andLet's PlayerOneyNGin the original English version, reviewer and fandubberSiendukin the Russian dub, and trope analystLe Tropeurin the French dub. Dark Horse Victory: He wins the Favorite Character Award despite having been created that very day for a joke, while Caine initially believed that he was the winner of the award.Ming:You shouldn't have assumed you won the award. Now we both look foolish. Dub Name Change: Justified as he only exists for the "ass-u-ming" joke which doesn't translate outside of English. On certain dubs, Ming's name has been changed in order to make the joke work:In the Dutch dub, he's calledRik.In the French dub, he's calledCubain, with the joke being changed to a pun onconcubin, in that it makes acon(ass) out of Cubain from Cuba.In the German dub, he's calledGerungand isfemale.In the Hungarian dub, he's calledBéni.In the Indonesian dub, he's calledAsu.In the Polish dub, he's calledPu, with the joke translating "assuming" toprzypuszczanieand the joke beingszczanie przy Pu(pissing by/next to Pu), which Pu is offended by.In the Russian dub, he's calledKiy.In the Spanish dub, he's calledMir, due to "assuming" being translated asasumir.In the Turkish dub, he's calledBenim.In the Ukrainian dub, he's calledDuke.

characters.name: Feral Monster
characters.description: A version of Gummigoo conjured by Caine to torture Pomni. Animalistic Abomination: He and his gang are turned into horrifying, abominated feral monsters that try to tear Pomni limb from limb. Beware the Silly Ones: A lovable gummy crocodile bandit becomes Caine's mindless attack dog. Brainwashed and Crazy: Everything of theLoveable Roguefrom his first appearance is gone, leaving behind only a feral predator venting Caine's fury. Butter Face: From the neck down, he looks like Gummigoo, but his head has realistic leathery scales and snarling teeth. Then the rest of him shapeshifts into an equally realistic-looking crocodile as he chomps down on Pomni's arm.

characters.name: Shadowy Figure
characters.description: A shadowy figure resembling Ragatha conjured by Caine for Ragatha's torture. Abusive Parents: It's heavily implied that this apparition is made to imitate Ragatha's abusive mother. Ambiguous Situation: It's never directly said what the shadow in Ragatha's torture is meant to represent. It is easy to assume it's her mother in a worst-case nightmare scenario based on Ragatha mentioning her and her habit of downplaying things, but it's also just as likely it could be something more abstract, like Ragatha's own fear of self sabotage, or some other aspect of herself - since it shares her hairstyle. Creepy Centipedes: A few centipedes are placed curled up on plates during Ragatha's nightmare sequence,adding to Ragatha's horror. Human Pincushion: It physically tortures Ragatha by throwing knives at her, including her eye and chest. A few other ragdolls are present at the table, also punctured by knives.

characters.name: Shadowy Trio
characters.description: A circle of cackling silhouettes of Pomni, Kaufmo, and Ribbit that surround Jax during Caine's torture sequence. Body Horror: In terms of physical torture, Jax suffers by far the most out of the Players with his skin being peeled off in a parallel to aShameful Strip. Does This Remind You of Anything?: They take the form of Jax's friends, who circle and mock him like a pack of bullies as one resembling Ribbit rips his skin off in a way evoking aShameful Strip. This scene becomes a clear metaphor for transmisogyny and fear of outing as Jax's trauma is explored the following episode. Flaying Alive: They tear off Jax's skin as easily as peeling a potato. The Freelance Shame Squad: Caine's personal torture for Jax is a revolving circle of shadowy apparitions shaped like his friends endlessly laughing at him.

characters.name: The Machine
characters.description: Achievements in Ignorance: During its rampage after Pomni presses its "STOP" button, The Machinesomehowmanages to suck in Kaufmo in the process and cure him of his abstraction, not looking any worse for wear. Too bad for Kaufmo that the skit The Machine appears in isn't canon. Agony Beam: Getting sucked in and transformed by The Machine is apparently a painful ordeal, according to Gangle. Ragatha and Pomni are later shown to be screaming in pain after getting spat out. This is played more forBlack Comedythan horror, especially since everyone seems to recover from it quickly afterwards. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: While initially claiming to want to grant the Players' greatest desires, Zooble eventually deduces The Machine just wants to spit out merch, regardless of whether the players actually are pleased with the outcome or not. Indeed, while Gangle appears okay being turned into her Manager form on the outside, she internally admits that the process was "so painful". Then there's Ragatha, who loses the ability to speak after being turned into plastic (which she didn't want to do, since she wished for a horse instead), and Pomni screams in horrorafter being turned into a pencil. Back from the Dead: The Machine ends up exploding in "PRESENTING MY FINEST WORK YET POMNI!" due to its desire to absorb as much as it can, but is perfectly fine afterwards. He also somehow manages to bring Kaufmo back from abstraction in the process. The Bogan: The Machine speaks withMaxmoefoe's natural Australian accent, and is a shrieking... machine that wants to turn everything it sucks up into merch.

characters.name: # — B
characters.description: 0% Approval Rating: As the architect of all the horrible-to-poorly-planned adventures of the Circus, the Players don'tlikeCaine so much as they have todealwith him. Even if he doesn't mean to hurt them or cause them to lose their minds, he is so boastful and sure of himself that he tends not to listen to others, abuse them, and generally make a nuisance of himself both directly and indirectly. Bubble, the NPC he spends the most time with, is implied to intentionally get on his nerves with their strange behavior and almost tells him todiebefore glitching into an erratic swearing suggestion of a beach party. It comes to a head by the Favorite Character Awards he decides to host, asdespite havingmadethe Committee ofNPCsthat love him vocally and unconditionally, he finds out hestill didn't get any votes.By the end of "Beach Episode",he strung along the players with what seemed to be a way out of the circus, only for it to be just an elaborate adventure, all in the desperate hopes that they would choose to remain in the circus and stay with him. Naturally, the circus crew isfuriousthat they were deceived, Jax especially, and any bit of good will they might've had left towards Caine likely vanished then and there. This culminates in "hjsakldfhl" leading topretty much every single one of the Circus mates (except Kinger, who wasindisposed), going into a collective"The Reason You Suck" Speechabout Caine's narcissism and sheer lack of empathy for his subjects,triggering his complete and utter meltdownbefore being accidentally deleted. That being said,noneof the playersare happy with the outcome. Caine makes a return in the finale, havingchanged for good, but also having understood that the players have every reason to still fear and distrust him. After beingBrought Down to Normal, showing the crew what their real-life counterparts are up to, and helping to truly make the circus a home for all of them, they finally make amends and consider Caine a part of the group. 11th-Hour

characters.name: Mike Dobby
characters.description: The leader ofC&A'sdevelopment team that was responsible for programming creative AI and Scratch's real-world counterpart. He was practically in a league of his own within his field, being widely recognized as a one-of-a-kind genius, though he had trouble describing his ideas to other people as they were noted to be quite abstract. His unique level of programming insight and difficulties with communication was potentially influenced by a brain tumor. It was likely because of this illness that Dobby at some point decided to create a brain scanner, which led to the creation of Caine's Digital Circus. For tropes related to Scratch, see his folderhere. The Ace: Dobby was a far superior programmer compared to Grant and was in a league of his own. This is Deconstructed; while he was a superior computer scientist, his means and methods were so unconventional that nobody else could really follow up on them. All for Nothing: He attempted to escape his death (in a sense) by creating a brain scanner, but not only was he unable to activate the mind files and had to deem the project a failure, Scratch, his digital footprint, became the very first Abstraction. Moreover, C&A would eventually fall under for one reason or another.If he didpass away from his cancer as Gooseworximplied, he essentially only succeeded at dyingtwice. Ambiguous Situation: While it's known he suffered from a brain tumor, it's never clarified if said tumor was benign (meaning as a noncancerous growth, it wouldn't spread to other parts of the body but still disrupt and influence critical functions in the mind) or malignant, though either case would have greatly impacted his life. Given that his scanner creates a digitizied copy of the mind, complete with the desire to mimic biological functions despiteno longer needing them, it can also be suggested he was preparing for any scenario with hisalready-abstractmindset. Gooseworx states that he "died horribly", implying his tumor was ultimately malignant and fatal

characters.name: Grant Best
characters.description: Kinger's real-world counterpart, and one of the C&A programmers that would ultimately be responsible for the creation of Caine. He has a wife named Destiny and two daughters named Anne and Sam. For tropes related to Kinger, see his pagehere. Babies Ever After: Played with. While it’s unknown when Grant and Destiny conceived Anne and Sam, it’s also never mentioned that they have children until the final episode’s resolution to solidify that Kinger’s counterpart is living a happy life. Boring, but Practical: But reallyonly relatively when compared to his colleague, Mike Dobby, whom he recognizes as a unique genius in the same field. While Mike's fateremains unknown, Grant has been discovered to still be around in the present with a mundane career in IT capable of supporting his family, instead of anything groundbreakingly convoluted like whateverC&Awas planning. Family Man: He still works in the technology field, but the happy life he has with his family is given more emphasis over his career.

characters.name: Abigail Brooks
characters.description: Pomni's real-world counterpart, an accountant who does urban exploration in her free time. She also runs aYouTubechannel calledAbbyAdventures57where she explores old, abandoned buildings, and also owns an Instagram account called abbybabblybrooks. For tropes related to Pomni, see her pagehere. Character Blog: She owns aYouTubechannel calledAbbyAdventures57, where she posts videos of her exploring old, abandoned buildings. She also owns an Instagram account called abbybabblybrooks. Commonality Connection: Sometime after unknowingly creating Pomni, Abigail made some new friends who also enjoy urban exploring and are happy to appear in her videos. Friendless Background: Had few friends growing up, although has recently gained some through her life as an urban explorer.

characters.name: Suzie J. Ackerman
characters.description: Ragatha's real-world counterpart. A real estate agent. For tropes related to Ragatha, see her pagehere. All Girls Like Ponies: Suzie grew up on a farm that had a lot of horses, and even after leaving and cutting ties with her abusive mother, she's still involved in equestrianism.The article about her in Caine's slideshowalso describes how Suzie became locally famous for preserving a large horse ranch after the patriarch of the owning family died by connecting them with a buyer who wanted to keep the property the way it was. All There in the Manual: Suzie's middle name is only given as an initial. It wouldn't be until Gooseworx confirms on Tumblr that her middle name is "Joanne". Ancestral Name:According to Gooseworx, her middle name is "Joanne", the same name as her mother.

characters.name: Zoey Raghavan
characters.description: Gangle's real-world counterpart. An aspiring webcomic artist. She dropped out of college and worked at a fast food shop before getting hit by a truck. Despite this, she made a fast recovery and went on to get a job at a small design agency and achieve her dreams of becoming a webcomic artist. She owns a Twitter account namedmoezoe26. For tropes related to Gangle, see her folderhere. Bollywood Nerd: She's a South Asian American and anOtakuwho aspires to create her own manga-inspired webcomic. Burger Fool: After dropping out of college, she worked at a fast food restaurant as a shift manager before she got hit by a truck one day. After she survived, Zoey decided to pursue her artistic dreams again, and was able to quit her fast food job for a design firm job and create a webcomic based on her time working in fast food. Character Blog: Owns a Twitter account namedmoezoe26, where she posts her art and some parts of her webcomic.

characters.name: Riley Verselis
characters.description: Zooble's real-world counterpart. They are the owner of the Triangle Bar. For tropes related to Zooble, see their folderhere. Art Reflects Personality: Riley decorated their bar by repurposing discarded items and with prints of queer icons they made themself, showing their eclectic and flexible style. Bartender Confidant: They're the friendly owner and head bartender of the Triangle Bar, knowing their regulars well and creating a safe LGBTQ-centric space for people to be themselves. Desperately Looking for a Purpose in Life: Based on Zooble's desire toleave a mark in the worldand the fact that they bounced around jobs frequently, it's implied that Riley was aimlessly searching for a calling they felt would be impactful prior to creating Zooble and found their calling in bartending afterward.

characters.name: Leeroy Mateo
characters.description: Jax's real-world counterpart. Acloseted young trans womanfrom a broken household who endured a divorce from her distant father and later abusive single mother. After getting into a physical altercation with her mother, she ran away from home and spent several months living on the streets before she moved in with a friend and got a job as a delivery driver. For tropes related to Jax, see his pagehere. Accidental Murder: Jax recalls the time when she pushed her mother to the ground out of fear when the latter tried to hug her, possibly inadvertently killing her. It's unknown if it actually did kill her, but Lee decided to run away afterwards. Although the fact Lee’s living a normal life at the end rather than in prison does imply her mother survived. Alive in the Alternate Universe: Lee was eventually able to get help, find supportive friends, and land a stable job as a delivery driver to pay rent. But although she now lives a happier life, sadly, the same can't be said for her digital counterpart, who pushed everyone away and Abstracted as a result. Alternate Personality Punishment: Inverted. Jax believes herself to be a terrible personBeyond Redemption, and remains Abstracted despite Pomni's best attempt to save her. Her real-life counterpart, Lee Mateo, got help and eventually recovered after months of being homeless. She made new friends and even got herself a job to pay her rent. Pomni and the others take solace in the fact that, while they were unable to save Jax herself, her source of origin at least received the help she needed and now lives a happier life.

characters.name: Destiny Best
characters.description: Grant's wife and Queenie's real-world counterpart. Together, they live with their two children, a pair of girls named Anne and Sam. For tropes related to Queenie, see her tropeshere. Alive in the Alternate Universe: Her digital counterpart abstracted years ago, while she’s alive and well in the present day. Ambiguous Situation: It's unknown whether Destiny worked for C&A too or was simply bought in by her husband to test the headset. Kinger does apologize to Queenie for roping her into this situation, but it still doesn't clarify anything. However, as far as Caine is concerned, her brain scan copy counts as part of the "first generation" of players (who largely consisted of C&A employees). Babies Ever After: Played with. While it’s unknown when Destiny and Grant conceived Anne and Sam, it’s also never mentioned that they have children until the final episode’s resolution to solidify that Queenie's counterpart is living a happy life.

characters.name: Leah and Doug
characters.description: Alive in the Alternate Universe: As the Circus is it’s own virtual reality, Leah and Doug are presumably still living their lives out in the real world, whereas their digital counterparts have long abstracted. Dark and Troubled Past: Leah cut ties with her Mormon parents after she moved out because it's implied they weren't accepting of theirAmbiguous Gender Identityand Leah herself didn't want to be Mormon. The Ghost: As their Circus counterparts had already abstracted prior to Caine's deletion and long before his change of heart, he doesn't include them in his presentation of the human lives. The Pastor's Queer Kid: Especially given how Ribbit/Leah was confirmed she/they by Gooseworx, Leah's backstory has heavy subtext of religious queerphobia. Ribbit, Leah's digital copy, mentions becoming estranged with their parents because they were devout Mormons, unlike her, and even though there have historically been a great number of queer Mormons, the church's doctrine denies the existence of non-binary genders and enforces strict gender roles. Riddle for the Ages: While we can discern the circumstances behind how most of the main cast entered the Circus, we never get an explanation for how and why these two discovered the Brain Scanner.

characters.name: Joanne Ackerman
characters.description: Suzie/Ragatha's mother, whom she had a rather strained relationship with. Abusive Parents: Everything we've heard about her thus far has revealed she heavily abused Suzie. Ragatha mentions that her main memories of her mother involve "yelling", "berating", and "guilt-tripping" and is pretty sure her mother doesn't miss her while she's in the circus. Episode 8 has Caine's torture room for Ragatha involve a shadowy apparition of her mother flinging knives at her. Ragatha is relieved to learn that Suzie successfully cut all ties with her sometime after her creation. All Take and No Give: Ragatha implies her relationship with her mother was like this, which is one of the main reasons for Ragatha's current issues. All There in the Manual: Her name is never revealed in the series, butinvokedWord of Godconfirmsthat her name is "Joanne". Ambiguous Situation:Ragatha may have had other siblings or family members that Ragatha's mother could've also been abusive to. "hjsakldfhl" shows other impaled ragdolls at the dinner table during Ragatha's torture sequence, but nothing is confirmed so far about what it may mean.Given the fact that Ragatha was trapped in the Digital Circus since 2008 (about 9 years In-Universe), it's unknown what has happened to her mother back in the real world or if she is even still alive. Ragatha believes her mother doesn't miss her, and it's clear from Ragatha's description that the feeling is mutual. The only mention we get for her in the finale is that Suzie cut off all contact with her at some point after she put on the headset, leaving her fate in the present day unknown.The exact extent of Joanne's abuse towards Suzie isn't made clear. She was at the very least emotionally abusive if the way Ragatha talks about her in "Untitled" is anything to go by. If Ragatha's nightmare sequence in "hjsakldfhl" is to be taken literally it would also imply that she was physically abusive too, though whether this is a 100% accurate depiction of Joanne's real-life

characters.name: Leeroy Mateo's Mother
characters.description: Lee/Jax's mother, with whom she had a strained, complex relationship. Abusive Personality Shift: Jax notes that her mother used to care for her, but after her dad left them, she changed and started taking her frustrations out on Lee. Ambiguous Situation: Why she hugged Lee after tearing into her for coming out as trans is unclear. She could'verealized she'd gone too farand tried to comfort her, but it's also possible thatshe was simply trying to manipulate Lee emotionally. Jax herself admits that she has no ideawhyher mother hugged her, and not knowing makes her feel worse about the whole thing. Asshole Victim: Deconstructed. Whether she is dead or not is unclear (but likely alive given that the cops never seem to have gone after Lee during the months where she was homeless and then got a job), but little to no sympathy is given to her after being such a hypocritical, abusive mother to her daughter after the divorce. Especially when she goes on a very angry, ugly verbal tirade on Lee about what's implied to be her coming out as trans, or in some way exploring femininity, only to suddenly turn a 180 by hugging him afterwards, leading to Lee understandably shoving her in a self-defense reflex. However, this still doesn't stop Lee from beinginstantly horrified by what she didand it's made clear that even years later, Jaxconsiders it one of her deepest regrets, regardless of how terrible her mother was. Chekhov's Gunman: She was briefly mentioned by Jax in passing during the "Poacher's Paradise" adventure in Episode 5.

characters.name: Leeroy Mateo's Father
characters.description: Lee/Jax's father, who left her and her mom when she was in high school. Ambiguous Situation:Why Mr. Mateo was neglectful to his daughter and eventually divorced his wife without seeing his daughter again is unclear. If Jax's words are accurate, Mr. Mateo simply gave up on raising Lee after seeing that "he" can't meet whatever standards he presumably has of "him." On the other hand, likely, Mr. Mateo didn'twantto be a father, and only raised Lee with his wife out of obligation before booking it once his daughter was old enough, given how Jax describes him as neglectful even before the divorce. The divorce also could have been more due to marital issues with his wife and he simply didn't care enough about Lee to keep in contact with her after the split.Jax mentions that after the divorce, her mother would accuse "him" of being just as bad as "his" father whenever "he" lashed out. It's unclear if this implies Mr. Mateo was worse than passively neglectful and possiblymistreated his wife(and perhaps more actively abusive to his daughter than Jax let on) or if Mrs. Mateo was just projecting her frustrations with their irreconcilable differences and typical arguments they might have had before the divorce. Why Mr. Mateo was neglectful to his daughter and eventually divorced his wife without seeing his daughter again is unclear. If Jax's words are accurate, Mr. Mateo simply gave up on raising Lee after seeing that "he" can't meet whatever standards he presumably has of "him." On the other hand, likely, Mr. Mateo didn'twantto be a father, and only raised Lee with his wife out of obligation before booking it once his daughter was old enough, given how Jax describes him as neglectful even before the divorce. The divorce also could have been more due to marital issues with his wife and he simply didn't care enough about Lee to keep in contact with her after the split. characters.name: Anne and Sam Best

characters.name: Jax - Tropes J to Z
characters.description: Jaw Drop:Played for Laughs. Upon hearing Zooble stating that they want the ability to have sex in "They All Get Guns", Jax gives a humorous, shocking expression with his mouth actually opening up. Jerkass Façade: At first glance, Jax is a cynical, narcissistic, and sadistic prankster who views the digital world as a consequence-free space for his personal entertainment and frequently torments other circus members for his own amusement. He trips over Ragatha in his teaser, constantly abuses Gangle like stepping on her comedy mask, shoving her, as shown in her teaser, and blackmailing her in "Candy Carrier Chaos!", pushes characters out of moving vehicles, and went far as putting centipedes in Ragatha's room in the pilot. Pomni and Zooble even call him an "asshole" on separate occasions. However, as the series progresses, it becomes clear that said behavioris actually a coping mechanism for being trapped in the digital world and losing his friends Ribbit and Kaufmo, seeking to push everyone away from him so he’llNever Be Hurt Again. And on top of that, it is ironicallythe very thing that is hurting him the most and driving him closer to - and ultimately past - the point of abstraction by isolating him from the other players, the very people that could help him. Jerkass Has a Point: Jax is an unapologetic asshole who happily stomps on other people's feelings, but he's rarelywrongwhen he tears into them instead of bullying them.At the beginning of the pilot, where Pomni enters the circus and of course asks for an exit, he interrupts Ragatha's struggle to find a soft way of telling herthere is no exitto bluntly state that. characters.name: Caine - Tropes I to Z
characters.description: I Just Want to Be Loved: Caine desires to be loved and praised by the players since he is the ringmaster and host of the Amazing Digital Circus.When he discovers that literallynobodyvoted for him in "Favourite Character Awards", he begins glitching out more and more. His entire scheme in "Beach Episode" is, at its core, an attempt at aSecret Test of Characterthat is supposed to push the players into showing how much they appreciate him, but it really only reveals how truly desperate he is for them to like him and just how far he is willing to go in his misguided attempts at winning their approval. Even in his final moments before his deletion in "hjsakldfhl", he furiously laments that all he ever desired was to carry out his function, and be praised for it.Caine:WHY DO YOU PEOPLE TORMENT ME?! I DIDN'TASKTO BE CREATED! I JUST WANTED TO FULFILL MY PURPOSE! I Just Want to Have Friends: Deconstructed. Despite being an AI, Caine is genuinelyIntrigued by Humanityand wants to learn how to get the Players accustomed to his adventures so that they can be good friends during their time together. However, due to a combination of his programming literally making it impossible for him to comprehend basic human needs and his personality of always having to be in control and be the one who decides what's fun, he unintentionally pushes the players away rather than creating any functional relationships with them, to the point where they barely tolerate his presence at best, which is best exemplified by no one voting for him at the Favorite Character Show. This comes to a head in "Beach Episode" whenhe tricks the Players into thinking they'll be able to flee the Circus when it was really just another one of his adventures, which leaves them angrier at him than ever, rather than enjoying spending more time with him.
